#4881. 9 Best At-Home Laser Hair Removal Devices of 2026, Tested by Women's Health Editors

Our favorites include Braun and Epilaser.

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

Fall is in full swing, but if you’re like us and prefer a smooth look year-round, you’ve likely tried all sorts of hair removal tools. Disposable razors are convenient, but dermatologist Caroline Robinson, MD, says they can cause microscopic nicks and irritation. Waxing provides immediate results, but the upkeep and the pain of simultaneously ripping out dozens of hairs from our legs are as painful as they sound. Enter at-home laser hair removal devices, which dermatologists and our hard-to-please editors swear by for their legs, bikini lines, underarms, and faces.

They zap unwanted hairs at their roots, significantly slowing regrowth and leaving skin smoother. While they don’t offer permanent hair loss, we’ve found the long-term effects are worth using one of these devices. After testing them for more than three years, we’re confident that you’ll also enjoy the long-term results they deliver. Most of these devices take anywhere from one to four weeks for initial results, and up to 12 weeks for full results to show. Starting now gives you enough time to ensure that you’re hair-free by your next vacation to these Travel Award-winning destinations.

Need more motivation to start now? It’ll take four weeks for visible results to show, which means if you start now, then you’ll notice a difference before your holiday travel, with better results by the time you enjoy a gorgeous fall wedding. So start your at-home laser hair removal treatments now, stay consistent, and by the time your next beach trip hits, you’ll forget what shaving even feels like.

So what makes laser hair removal devices worthy of a spot in your busy routine? They have an upfront time commitment: you have to initially use one up to five times a week. But after a few months, your upkeep routine drops significantly to once or twice each season. They’re also more cost-effective than professional treatments. Hear us out: A laser that costs $500 is basically the same price as a professional hair removal session, and the results from that in-office treatment won't last forever, but you will continue using your at-home laser for years.

Ahead, we asked seven dermatologists about how to shop for laser hair removal devices and their no-fail product recommendations. They also answered your most burning questions in our FAQ section after our product highlights.

Meet the Skin I-Expert, a Braun laser hair removal device that we’ve been testing since January 2024. Given our long-term positive experience using this tool, we knew it was the clear winner of our best overall distinction.

For starters, most laser hair removal devices have about 200,000 flashes or the equivalent of 780 at-home treatments, Dr. Nazarian previously told us in our guide to the best facial hair removal devices. This IPL device has double that, aka 1,560 treatments, meaning the investment will last for several years even with consistent use. Each hair removal sesh will only cost you $0.31, which is a third of the price of a Wet n Wild eyeliner.

Next, it’s our only recommended device that connects to a compatible smartphone app via Bluetooth and Wi-Fi technology to tailor your treatment to your needs. Wohlner was impressed with how well the intuitive app assessed her skin tone and hair color for compatibility.

Wohlner admits that she never used interchangeable heads before because they were intimidating. However, Braun solved that problem because the app told her what head to use for different parts of her body. The software even analyzes how much coverage Wohlner needs to ensure she doesn't miss any spots. Lastly, the app has a built-in calendar, so she’ll always remember when she’s due for some zaps—something Wohlner admits can be hard to keep track of, but is key for results.

Like other Braun laser hair removal devices we've tried, this one comes in a sturdy carrying case that keeps everything neatly organized under your vanity, or wherever you choose to store it. The unit doesn't call out any specific cooling technology, but Wohlner said her experience was largely pain-free. "I felt a little zippiness here and there, but nothing I could actually describe as painful—more like a super quick, tiny pinch," she says.

As for the results, they were solid. Wohlner typically shaves her self-described super coarse hair daily until she started using this device. She was impressed that she didn’t need to shave her underarms for weeks after her first treatment. "After three more sessions, I saw a pretty major payoff,” says Wohlner. “There are definitely a few hairs still popping through, but they've grown back so slowly."

Overall, this device is pricey, but for someone serious about tackling the hair on their body—whether armpits, legs, Brazilian area, and beyond—it's worth every penny, especially if you feel like you could use a little help through the process.

Truly the only thing we don’t enjoy about this device is the price tag. However, it has 400,000 flashes—double the average of our other favorite devices—which means this Braun can easily last you 30 years. Genius!

If you can't stomach the price of Braun's latest and greatest IPL, the brand’s cheaper Silk Expert Pro 5 is hardly a downgrade. In our comprehensive test, Earley found the device to be both easy to use and highly effective.

The Silk Expert Pro 5 removes all of Earley’s unwanted hair after just four weeks of use. "I was so happy to say goodbye to my leg and armpit hair,” says the working mom of four. “Anything that saves me time—and trust me, not having to shave is a huge time-saver—is something I'm 100% willing to invest in." The ergonomic handle is easier to hold than the bulky, cheaper alternatives that remind her of hair dryers. For larger areas of her body, Earley holds down the trigger for continuous flashes—a feature she says speeds things up immensely.

Compared to our best overall pick, the Silk Expert Pro 5 lacks convenience features like a compatible smartphone app that allows you to tailor your treatments and track coverage areas to make sure you don't miss any spots. It does, however, have a proprietary SensoAdapt technology, which uses a built-in sensor to continuously and automatically read your skin tone and self-adjust the energy setting for safety and efficacy just like its more expensive counterpart.

Overall, it's a worthy pick—as evidenced by Earley’s testing experience and its popularity on Amazon and TikTok—if you're looking to spend a little bit less and don't mind sacrificing a few features.

We’ve been testing and liking Ulike devices since 2022. From the ULike Sapphire Air+ to the Air 3, and now the featured Air 10 is the brand’s latest model worth owning.

Instead of buying two devices, the Air 10 works quite literally from your face to your toes. The latest version is equipped with dual lights to zap hair on your upper lip, bikini area, underarms, and legs. It offers four modes, including a new setting for stubborn hairs. The gentle intensity setting zaps hair from the face, while the strongest mode uses high-speed flashes to speed up removing unwanted face and body hair.

What we like most is that Air 10 is easy to use and relatively pain-free. While other devices use heat to remove hair, the Ulike Air 10 cools itself down to 65 degrees Fahrenheit. This chilly surface helps lower your skin temperature to prevent irritation and burns from overheating. Maberry says the cooling tech found in both the Air 3 and Air 10 models is especially useful for sensitive areas like the bikini line.

It’s also a relatively low time commitment of 20 to 30 minutes for a full treatment while watching TV. "Once you get the hang of how to use the device, it's super easy to zap, zap, zap while you scroll through TikTok,” Maberry said in her review. Ulike promises visible results within four weeks, but Maberry saw her hair thin in just three weeks. The hair-free appearance was so dramatic around week six that Maberry was tempted to stop the treatments entirely. She continued using it for the recommended 12 weeks and now hairs only pop up every four to six weeks.

One thing to note: the built-in cooling fan is a bit noisy, so Maberry turns up her TV volume slightly. Still, the tradeoff isn’t a real dealbreaker: "I would rather have a painless device that makes little noise than a silent one that causes a burning sensation," she said. It’s also worth mentioning that this device is best suited for someone with fair to olive complexions and brown to black hair. The tech can’t accurately differentiate between a deeper skin tone and dark tresses.

This budget-conscious device seems a little too good to be true, but it earned a casual 4-star average from nearly 12,900 Amazon reviews. More than 7,330 of these reviews are a perfect 5-star rating. Not too shabby! Shoppers rave about using this IPL device on their face and body, including the ultra-sensitive bikini line.

Like other laser hair removal devices, this IPL tool features a manual mode that emits a single flash at a time to precisely target areas, like the chin, upper lip, and armpits. There is also an auto mode that emits continuous flashes for the legs, stomach, and arms. And FWIW, this device comes with an epic 36-month warranty and 100-day money-back policy, which is more than triple the regular return window of other Amazon beauty products.

The main complaint about this price-friendly tool is that it’s bulky, making it less ideal for travel. However, it does boast an ergonomic design for an overall comfortable hair removal experience. And since each treatment area requires a maximum of two minutes or less, you won’t have to worry about any discomfort for your wrist.

If you’re like us, then you’re probably a bit surprised that an at-home laser hair removal device can be so costly. However, we put this one to the test for nearly two months and saw major results. Based on our long-term testing experience, Epilaser’s effective tech, and the sophisticated design and feel, we knew it was deserving of a spot on this list. We adored it so much that we featured it as one of the best beauty launches of 2025 in our annual Skincare Awards package.

Our deputy visual director, Dangi McCoy, usesd this laser two to three times a week for two months on her right underarm to compare the results. She noticed the treated area regrew hair more slowly, and had half the amount of underarm hair compared to her left side. “At seven weeks, I’m still using the laser, but the regrowth has been so sparse I could count the hairs at a glance,” McCoy said in her Epilaser review.

Notably, this is the only featured device that use diode lasers for hair removal. As a quick reminder, using the wrong laser type, aka IPL, can cause burns in dark brown and deep skin tones. Thankfully, the Epilaser’s diodes prevent this from happening. The device’s unique laser wavelength bypasses the melanin that gives our skin its pigment, allowing it to safely remove hair rather than mistaking our skin for dark hair.

Epilaser is also extremely functional when you have limited outlets in your home or hotel room. During McCoy’s testing process, she found some of the cords to be cumbersome, so it was nice to have the flexibility of charging her device and using it cordless. It also allowed McCoy to remove hair from anywhere in her home, such as the couch while watching Uptown Girls.

OK, so what about the discomfort? Is splurging really worth it in this case? Turns out, yes! Epilaser maximizes hair removal results even if you have a low tolerance for discomfort. While no laser hair removal device is completely painless, McCoy only felt occasional quick pricks on her skin. The brand’s proprietary SPOT technology zaps up to 15 hairs per second, while leaving your skin untouched.

She was also impressed by how lightweight the cordless Epilaser felt in her hands. The device feels sturdy, and its ergonomic design enhances comfort during longer treatment sessions. Plus, this laser hair removal device looks absolutely gorgeous IRL—the bronze-tone trim truly elevates the luxurious appearance.

Given the laser’s smaller opening, you can even use this device on your face. It also comes with a soft-sided travel case with a short handle strap that’s easy to pack in your carry-on or rolling suitcase.

SmoothSkin's system works for anyone who wants something that's easy to use and doesn't require a lot of manual work or tinkering with buttons or various features. A patented sensor measures your skin before each flash and automatically selects the light best suited to your skin tone. This helps speed up the whole process, so full-body treatments take approximately 10 minutes.

It also includes a precision head to target smaller areas of the body—like the bikini line or even the upper lip or chin. The adaptable head also makes it easier to follow along your natural curves, like your kneecaps or underarms.

Like other great laser hair removal devices on the market, this one promises visible hair reduction in as little as four weeks and complete results by 12 weeks. It works so well that you’ll notice a difference after just one use, which is a true testament to this laser's power. SmoothSkin is on the pricey side, but justified by the fact that it offers unlimited flashes, allowing you to use this device for life. Overall, an excellent value over its lengthy lifetime. No wonder it earned 250 five-star Amazon reviews.

You've probably seen this popular laser hair removal device on your social media feeds, and our team says it really does live up to the hype. Nood’s proprietary PrecisionPulse laser makes all of the difference. The IPL flashes every 10 milliseconds, meaning it exposes your skin to less light that could accidentally cause burns.

Nood’s combination of continuous flashes and larger window make it better suited for larger areas, especially the legs. You can polish them off in 15 to 20 minutes, though it's harder to target smaller areas, like the upper lip. We also love the large digital display on this model.

It makes it very easy to toggle through the seven different intensity levels, and it's always clear which one you're working on. The price is friendlier than some other options, plus the brand offers a 90-day money-back guarantee, which makes this device a great option for anyone on the fence about at-home laser hair removal.

There are a lot of laser hair removal devices on the market, which is why you should consider a few of these pointers before investing.

IPL and diode lasers both slow hair growth and reduce the thickness of individual strands by scanning for pigment and targeting the hair follicle, says dermatologist Melanie Kingsley, MD. But, they each have their benefits and limitations.

IPL is the most commonly used type of light in at-home laser hair removal devices. This technology uses broad-spectrum light to target melanin, the pigment that gives your hair its color. The light is also unsuitable for dark and deep skin tones because it can’t distinguish between melanin-rich skin and the pigment of dark hair, says dermatologist Rachel Nazarian, MD. However, if you have a fair to olive complexion with dark hair, then you’re an ideal candidate for IPL treatments.

Until recently, all at-home laser hair removal devices were IPL lasers. But Epilaser has a game-changing laser for home use. Unlike IPL lights, which emit a broad spectrum of light ranging from 400 to 1,400 nm, diode lasers are unique because they use a more concentrated wavelength of light (around 810 nm). This precise wavelength means it can better target the hair follicles rather than accidentally burning your skin, making it more accessible for some people with darker complexions.

Both are effective, but diode lasers are slightly more versatile. That said, no matter which one you go with, you’ll need multiple treatments to maintain your hair-free results.

One of the biggest considerations is the number of flashes a device is equipped to deliver. This number indicates how long the device will last, according to Dr. Nazarian. "Many devices contain about 200,000 flashes, which is typically good for more than 15 years, although it also depends on how many areas you’re treating," she says. Other recommendations on this list, like the Smoothskin, have unlimited flashes, which means they'll theoretically last forever, but are pricier.

Extra features like multiple intensity modes—lower options for sensitive skin; higher settings for those who want to see results fast (see the Nood)—or interchangeable heads for precise treatment all over the body (hi, Braun) can increase the price. The amount you spend comes down to the features you want in your device and how long you want it to last.

One of the best ways to reduce discomfort during laser hair removal is to use cooling technology. It lowers your skin’s temperature—before, during, and after each laser pulse—to help you better tolerate longer and higher treatment settings safely.

Devices with bigger heads are more efficient on large areas. For more targeted flashes, opt for rigs with compact heads, such as the Iouniya Laser Hair Removal, which can be used on both the face and body. If you have sensitive skin, consider stretching your treatments out to once a month to start and gradually up the frequency once your skin can handle the laser hair removal treatment. The final hair-free results will take longer to achieve but at least you won’t risk irritating your skin. FWIW, she says you’ll notice thinning hair after your first four treatments.

Once you choose your device, know that it can take some time to see results. While every device is different, you’ll probably use it weekly anywhere from four to 10 weeks before noticing lasting results, says dermatologist Bertha Baum, DO. The final results might take longer to achieve, but you won’t risk irritating your skin. FWIW, warm weather likely won’t return until April or early May, meaning you’ve got several weeks to achieve smooth results. Either way, Dr. Baum says you’ll notice thinning hair after your first four treatments.

This technology has come a long way and, while pricey, it's a long-term investment that pays for itself. Think of it this way: A laser that costs $500 is basically the same price as a professional hair removal session, and that in-office treatment won't last forever, but you will continue using your at-home laser for years. And FWIW, we found a few discounted, top-rated Amazon picks that start at just $42, but you’ll want to hurry since these are fleeting deals.

At Women’s Health, we prioritize hands-on editor testing to ensure you don’t waste your time or money. Ahead is insight on what went into our editorial process while trying the latest and greatest at-home laser hair removal devices.

After testing these devices since February 2022, beauty director Brian Underwood, deputy deals and trends editor Eunice Lucero-Lee, and luxury commerce editor Sarah Maberry whittled down this list to 12 of the best laser hair removal devices. We also tapped contributors Jasmine Gomez, Lily Wohlner, and Brigitt Earley to ensure these devices work across most skin tones.

They all boast impressive features, are comfortable to use, and offer incredible value. Plus, these picks are FDA-cleared, so they’ve been evaluated for safety and efficacy. Several dermatologists also shared their no-fail laser hair removal tips and best-in-class product recommendations.

And because we know what it’s like to ball on a budget, we also considered pricing. TBH, laser hair removal devices aren’t exactly cheap. Many cost between $300 and $600, especially when shopping for these expert-approved devices from well-respected brands, such as Braun.

To help, I carefully researched dozens of other cheaper, yet top-rated Amazon laser hair removal devices. Ultimately, I found four Amazon picks that are aligned with expert guidance and are currently discounted as low as $35. Talk about major savings! For added peace of mind, they all earned thousands of rave reviews from real Amazon customers.

So if you're ready to ditch daily shaving and bi-monthly waxing, we're confident—based on our own testing and our dermatologists' advice—that this list contains only the best, most effective options on the market worth your hard-earned coins.

Dr. Nazarian confirms at-home laser hair removal devices are generally safe and effective, citing a 2019 paper. The biggest challenge with many at-home devices comes down to their inability to differentiate between dark skin and dark hair due to their pigmentation. Melanin-rich complexions risk absorbing too much laser energy that increases the risk for burning, cautions Dr. Nazarian. If this is you, then see your dermatologist for a recommendation on the best laser hair removal treatments and devices.

It's also a good idea to do a patch test and not expose the treated area to sunlight for a week, says Dr. Shirazi. Your treated skin is temporarily more sensitive, and you risk sunburn, hyperpigmentation, and delayed healing. She also doesn’t suggest using the laser on tanned and tattooed skin, open wounds, moles, or birthmarks to avoid changing their appearance or causing accidental burns.

Truthfully, they're not optimal for sensitive or dark skin. Many at-home devices cannot distinguish between melanin-rich complexions and dark hair, says dermatologist Corey L. Hartman, MD. Anyone else can still give them a try.

And, like with salon treatments, it's important to practice patience—this isn't a "one and done" situation. Many devices need to be used multiple times weekly to achieve the initial results. Plus, each at-home session can take 10 to 60 minutes, depending on how much body and facial hair you plan to remove. While a tad annoying upfront, this minor inconvenience has a major payoff because your hair will regrow slower over time with regular use.

#4880. 9 Best Duvet Covers: Editor Sets to Style a Bedscape (2026)

Besides pieces like quilts and coverlets, I always say duvet covers are the best accessories to give a bedscape a bit more personality. Take it from Ariel Kaye, founder of juggernaut bedding brand Parachute, who has filled her eclectic LA home with a range of duvet covers that span vibrant, breezy linens to neutral, crisp percales.

To truly find the best of the best, I rounded up a group of writers and editors to test duvet covers from our favorite bedding brands—featuring muted, structured covers for minimalists and trendy colorways and patterns for maximalists. As for our top pick, we went with Boll & Branch’s Signature Hemmed Duvet Set since it’s organic, has a smooth and breathable feel, and comes in tons of prints and colors for easy styling.

If you’re still on the fence about what to go with for your bedroom, I also tapped AD PRO Directory designers to share what they look for in duvet covers, including materiality and design. Read below to create your dream bedscape this season.

For consistency, all prices listed reflect queen-size duvets unless otherwise noted, but up to king sizes are available for purchase from each brand.

Boll & Branch is one of AD’s favorite brands when it comes to bedding. With super soft sheets and other products made from 100% organic cotton, they have a heavy focus on sustainability and directly sourcing raw materials. The duvet cover follows suit, with long-staple cotton making for a durable piece of bedding that I’ve found is breathable enough for both hot and cold nights.

This organic-cotton duvet set can please pretty much anyone with a traditional bedroom. It has a tried-and-true cotton sateen material that gets softer with every wash, and designs—including subtle botanical prints—that are a must for anyone with classic taste. The earthy tones are great for a grounded bedroom too.

Bring the outdoors in with your styling by pairing one of Boll & Branch’s botanical prints with a textured linen sheet set.

Shop AD editors have stood behind Boll & Branch for years because of the brand’s sustainable business model and high-quality bedding. The signature cotton sheets have even earned a top spot in our best-of guides for the last five years. Just like these sheets, shopping producer Lauren Arzbaecher tells me that this Boll & Branch duvet cover’s sateen weave has a buttery soft texture. “The cotton is very smooth, and I maintained a comfortable temperature throughout the night even when bundled up underneath all my bedding,” she says. As a cold sleeper, Arzbeacher loves layering extra throws and blankets on top of her duvet, and she says this ultra-breathable material has all the “cuddly qualities” you’d want without making you overheat. Even better, the bedding is 100% organic, so you can rest knowing you’re not breathing in any harmful chemicals.

This sateen duvet cover also has a zipper closure, so it’s a lot easier for Arzbaecher to slip her Company Store down insert on and off than other button-closure covers she’s tried. “Their solid color range has a lovely mix of earthy hues, and the brand has been releasing more and more patterns, from stripes to florals,” for styling a bed, she adds.

I’m not sure what’s left to say about this bedding brand that hasn’t already been plastered across subway ads or Instagram feeds, but in short, Brooklinen is somewhat of a bedding celebrity. It has garnered cool-kid status by offering top-quality products using Oeko-Tex-certified products at reasonable prices.

The Classic Duvet Cover is made of percale, which can be compared to a crisp cotton button-down shirt. It’s soft and sophisticated in a matte, buttery finish that can be attributed to long-staple cotton fibers that are spun to make stronger but finer yarn.

We are not only big fans of Brooklinen products for their breathable, sustainable materials but also for their versatile designs. With 20 earthy tones, I recommend this duvet cover for any type of bedroom style—but I’d lean towards purchasing for a coastal design because of the soothing colors and prints.

Like Alpert, who has this duvet cover in her bedroom, I recommend styling it with textured linen sheets for a contrasting yet comfortable fabric combination and a throw blanket in complementary neutral and oceanic hues.

Not one but two AD writers love this Brooklinen cotton duvet cover all year long. Shopping writer Julia Harrison calls this super, super soft and very cool to the touch. “It stays cool even when I’ve wrapped myself all the way in it like a caterpillar so I’m never overheating, but I am staying comfy and warm,” she shares. Contributor Yelena Moroz Alpert says this is her favorite duvet cover of all time, hands-down, because of its unmatched airy and parachute-like quality. “The percale duvet cover has this smooth feel but at the same time it is remarkably light and crisp,” she says. “Apparently, it’s all because of the high-quality single-ply yarns, which are made from strong, long-staple cotton fibers that give it that buttery touch.”

The style potential is a plus here too. Alpert loves the “oyster” print since it strays away from more expected patterns like stripes filling up her linen closet. She got the matching sheets in the same print for this exact reason, saying the swirls remind her of “Hokusai’s waves and stand out in the sea of florals and plaids” in her linen closet.

From pajamas to sheets, Cozy Earth is a favorite of ours—and Oprah thanks to frequent appearances in her Favorite Things lists—for cooling bedding made of bamboo fabric. Its offerings also ring in at a budget-friendly price (especially with the brand’s frequent sales).

Many of the colors in Cozy Earth’s collection are grounded in the earth (to be expected). With this in mind, I see this duvet cover in a minimalist, bohemian, or coastal bedroom. Alpert’s peony pick is just as nice for a romantic bedroom or something seasonal for summer.

The delicate nature of the bedding (both in texture and color) makes it a striking contrast against crisp, patterned accents, like a percale floral sheet set.

When I asked Alpert what her favorite qualities are about Cozy Earth’s signature, silky duvet cover, there were almost too many to count. “This duvet cover is a trifecta of perks: It looks good, feels good, and won’t slip off the comforter,” she says. “But if I had to pick one, I’d say that I love the delicate pink hue and the equally delicate feel of the cover—just looking at my bed makes me want to crawl into it.”

The material (100% viscose from bamboo) has a breathable and smooth feel to it that’s nice for hot sleepers but also anyone who doesn’t want a more textured cover like linen. Even better, the soft, pastel-inspired color options like peony pink and laurel green make it a great fit for styling a bed during this blooming season. “The fabric is so delicate and dreamy that it reminds me of flower petals,” Alpert tells me. “Since I chose the peony colorway, it definitely fits the romantic profile.”

Even though it has a smooth texture, the comforter inside won’t slip around because of the secure snap closures. “Cozy Earth has 12(!) points of contact between the comforter and the cover, so there is no way anything is going to get loose, especially because these are snapped on, and not tied, like many other duvet covers,” she says. “I pair it with the bamboo viscose comforter with standard fill and the combination works great because the comforter has some weight and the duvet cover does not mess with it in any way.”

A darling of the 2010s direct to consumer movement, Parachute is a home brand best known for its bedding, though the company has also dabbled in furniture, mattresses, and other essentials. Its products, including the Linen Duvet Cover, are Oeko-Tex Standard 100–certified, meaning that every element (even buttons!) has been tested for substances damaging to human health. Parachute also doesn’t artificially soften their products. In the wrong hands, linen can be itchy or stiff until it’s been broken in, but that wasn’t the case here. This version, made of European Flax and made in the Guimarães region of Portugal, was inviting and oh so soft. The company also touts the material as naturally antimicrobial, which is a plus.

Another pick for a bohemian bedroom, this duvet cover has a lived-in look and several organic colors to choose from.

If you, in true minimalist fashion, like a monochrome bedscape, style this duvet cover with linen sheets in natural colors. If you want a slightly moodier bedroom, try a shade like cacao or indigo.

Contributor Lila Allen has nothing but good things to say about the feel of this linen and its nonchalant elegance: “I was pleasantly surprised at how soft this cover was—with linen, sometimes it can be a roll of the dice. This set had the best of both worlds: super supple but still casually elevated. The linen is a nice thickness, too; I can’t see any trace of the duvet inside of it.” Parachute’s linen has 175 GSM, and Quince’s linen that I mention down below has around 150 GSM. To Allen’s point, this means Parachute’s is more durable with a substantial feel and less opaque (the reason why she can’t see her duvet insert peeking through) with a lighter cover color like toast or sand.

Allen pairs her duvet cover with an all-season comforter from Riley, which she says stays secure through a button closure on the side and gives just the right amount of rumple together. The insert moves around a bit inside of the cover but mostly remains in place. “Best of all, I’ve been sleeping soundly with the set on hot nights as well as ones where the AC has been on overdrive, and so far it holds up in both situations—not too warm or cool.” Allen tells me that she shares a bed with her “hot-blooded husband and a large Maine Coon cat,” so her bed usually runs warm. This layerable, snuggly cover is perfect.

The home brand is headquartered in New York City, however, the materials are sourced from fourth-generation, family-owned textile mills in Portugal and other countries across Europe. The products span a range of bedding and bath products, namely duvet covers, sheets, towels, mats, and other accessories like pillows and robs.

Since all of the duvet covers come in neutral, unfussy colors, this is a great option for minimalists.

I style this simply with other neutrals like white or cream sheets. When I want to add more visual interest, I layer in butter yellow bedding or a quilt in soft, muted tones.

To put it simply, this duvet cover feels like a lightweight cashmere sweater. It’s not stuffy, but it’s not flimsy either. Riley Home’s somehow managed to make a cover that feels airy enough for nights when my apartment’s radiator runs overly hot and still warm enough when I want to curl up in bed after a cold commute from work.

Even though it feels soft, it’s not made of pure cashmere. In reality, it’s made of 95% cotton and just 5% cashmere, but I wouldn’t have noticed if I didn’t read the label so closely. The texture has a brushed quality to it that feels gentle and light on my skin. There are a few neutral colors on the site. I went with the oatmeal and have liked styling it with white sheet sets so far for a simple, not-overly-done-up bedspread. A couple of other thoughtful details are the interior ties and buttons to keep my comforter from shifting inside. The super-easy care sold me too. The brand doesn’t recommend dry cleaning—just a machine wash and dry with a gentle detergent will do. As someone who has lugged specialty cashmere bedding to NYC cleaners on foot through the years, this note in and of itself almost convinced me to give the bedding a try.

Quince’s entire deal is about making high-quality luxury products at an affordable price. They work only with factories that are both sustainable and pay a fair wage, which is something that many shoppers care enough about to pay a little extra for, but Quince cuts back on things like fancy packaging to keep costs down.

Quince is another AD favorite for its plethora of prints and solid colors. Try this duvet cover in your space—no matter its design style—for a lightweight addition to your bedscape that’s also budget friendly.

Since linen makes a statement on its own with its lived-in look, I recommend styling this duvet cover with Quince’s classic European linen sheet set and a fluffy duvet insert in moody neutral hues (think deep brown) for a cozy sleep oasis. It’s also neutral enough that you can add some pattern sheeting for extra personality.

I’ve had this Quince linen duvet for about a year and it’s been a mainstay since it’s substantial and textured while still having an airiness to it—even when I’m layering with a few throw blankets or quilts when it’s cold outside. Sometimes linen gets a bad rap for its rough texture, but this best seller has been gentle against my skin and only gotten softer with more routine wear and care. It’s not as soft as something like an heirloom-quality stonewashed linen, but I’m not too picky in the linen department. I think its Oeko-Tex certification gives it a leg up generally to some competitors in this fabric category too.

I chose this Quince duvet since there were so many color options to choose from. I love moody colors year-round, and the burgundy is true to the deep color I saw on the site and it hasn’t faded after months of washes. It has the relaxed look you know and love with linen materials. Steaming it knocks out wrinkles easily whenever I want a more put-together look in my bedroom, though.

At this price point and with the most colors and prints available in this guide, I think this comforter cover can give you a great, budget-friendly way to dress a bed. The button closures also help keep a duvet insert or comforter in place. The care has been simple. I wash it with similar colors on a cold cycle and tumble dry on low and have only noticed a loose thread here and there, but nothing too crazy.

As mentioned above in our top overall pick, Brooklinen is known as the “home of the internet’s favorite sheets,” so we find it to be a worthy destination for quality bedding—including this quilt-like duvet cover made with 100% cotton.

With a design that mirrors the appearance of a quilt, we think this duvet cover would dress a vintage-inspired space beautifully—like the bedding you’d find in a historic Victorian home.

Alpert chose the plum colorway because of its sophisticated look that anchors her bedroom. She shares that the hue looks exceptionally well-paired with the deep caramel of the Boll & Branch Grand waffle blanket, as the color almost works like a moody neutral.

Even though the Brooklinen website describes this duvet as “breezy,” Alpert says it feels more like a weighted blanket. “The ribbed side is certainly quilt-like, which is not surprising because each ribbon that runs through the duvet cover is padded ever so slightly,” she shares.

The cover has a two-sided design: one side with textured, ribbed matelasse and the other with a crisp percale fabric. Alpert thinks this material combo is genius since it keeps the duvet cover from feeling too heavy. “This is especially key for anyone who sleeps without a flat sheet—you’ll feel like you’re getting into freshly changed linens night after night,” she says. “On the flip side, the ribbed texture elevates the duvet cover, not only in how it looks but it gives your bedding a slightly cushy sensation.”

Rest assured that the feel isn’t as heavy as an actual weighted blanket. Alpert says it certainly has substance and structure, though. “When I sleep with it on, it feels as if I am very secure—no one will dare wake me up,” she notes.

Hommey is a relatively new Australian-based brand that got its start in 2020. It became popular for robes and nightwear in bold, fashionable stripes. The designs are now spread across the bedding category, including cotton and linen sheets and duvet covers.

Since the brand is known for more out-of-the-box colorways across its collections, this duvet color is a great option for maximalists looking to experiment with bold color-blocking.

For a moodier bedscape, I style this duvet cover with sheets in a deep tone like burgundy. Overall, the chocolatey hue acts like a neutral and pairs beautifully with lighter sheet colors like oatmeal, which can also complement the cream-colored trim.

I know we’ve talked about linen a couple of times already in this story, but Hommey’s duvet helps hit the trifecta for the category. The natural flax fiber felt smoother and more broken-in than my Quince version right out the package. My guess is that it’s because of the stonewashed finish, which is known to give scratchy linen a more silky quality. I won’t get ahead of myself and say it feels like pure silk, but I can confirm that it’s soft and breathable almost like an organic cotton duvet after a few washes. The duvet caught my attention even more because of all of the styles. There are over 30 fashionable colors and prints, like the oxford and plum reversible cotton duvet I want in a button-down shirt version. The linen offering has four distinct colorways, including the brown sugar with cream trim that I got for myself. I like deep colors for my bedscape, especially as the year starts inching towards fall and winter, and its rich hue hasn’t disappointed. It's the perfect complement to my autumnal color palette, especially when I pair it with burgundy linen sheets.

It is less expensive than the Parachute pick and has a plusher texture than the Quince, so I’d say this is the perfect middle ground for an approachable but high-quality linen duvet.

Garnet Hill was founded in New Hampshire in the mid-1970s by Pegge and Grant Dowse who built the brand on a commitment to sustainable materials, thoughtful craftsmanship, and responsible sourcing with products like organic cotton and flannel bedding. The bedding blends traditional styles with a modern touch to fit in a range of bedrooms.

Our tester says the Pear Garden print is completely unexpected. “As much as I love florals, stripes, and gingham, a girl needs a break…and these charming pears are just the right motif,” Alpert shares. “They signal a cottagecore moment without going over the top. Every time I glimpse the cheery yellow fruit, I crack a little smile. Plus, the colorway of bold yellow, sage green, brown, and cream are easy to coordinate with the rest of my bedding collection.”

Because the pear motifs are the statement, we think you can go with more subtle sheets like a white set with embroidered trim. If you’re more of a maximalist, you can lean into the pattern play with a gingham sheet set in a complementary muted tone like brown and extra layers like a faux fur blanket if you’re cozying up for winter.

According to Alpert, this duvet cover is synonymous with cozy. It’s the softest option on this list because of the brushed flannel fabric, and it’s also a great pick if you live in cold climates since it has a bit of heft to it. “It’s as if a layer of leaves, or in this case pears, is surrounding me during winter hibernation,” she says. “That’s in part because this specific flannel is woven to have a substantial six-ounce weight.”

Alpert’s had this for nearly one year and says it has a decadent texture, likening it to climbing under a layer of meringue when she pairs it with her fluffy Ostermoor down duvet insert. “The plush feel of the cover also makes me think that I’ve just scored an upgrade to a royal suite,” Alpert adds.

At this point, she hasn’t noticed any pilling, but she does note that the cover is a bit snugger than a typical king, so you can expect the duvet to feel a little loftier than a regular fit.

What to Look for in the Best Duvet Covers

A duvet cover is more than just a bedcover. This eye-catching textile has a large footprint in any bedroom and can instantly give your space a refresh—whether with unique colors and prints or something more modest—especially if you want to disguise an old duvet insert. With this in mind, I tapped AD PRO Directory designers to weigh in on what to look for in a duvet cover to elevate your bedroom.

Material: When it comes to duvet covers, everyone has their own personal preferences. For Nicole R. Fisher, CEO and founder of Nicole Fisher Interiors, it’s linen: “They’re effortless, lightweight, and airy. I think the simplicity of the linen transcends different styles and spaces,” she says. Fisher notes that the feel is a big factor when selecting a duvet cover.

Carmen René Smith, founder and principal designer of Aquilo Interiors, says that it also needs to feel soft to the touch, breathable, and cozy. “What’s the point of a beautiful duvet if you don’t want to snuggle into it?” she says. “Texture is key too—whether it’s silky, crisp, or nubby, it should add depth to the space.”

Comfort: All of the interior designers I spoke to for this story point to natural fibers, not only because of their quality but also their airflow and breathability. Shelbie Cox of Shelbie Cox Studio recommends natural fibers like organic cotton and linen and notes that polyester and other synthetic fibers are best to avoid since they can trap heat.

Design: With so many patterns and colors to choose from, it’s important to keep your bedroom’s design style in mind. If you like more of a minimalist bedroom, Cox suggests a fine stripe pattern (like Quince’s European Linen Duvet Cover) or a monochromatic, muted color palette (see the Cozy Earth Bamboo Duvet Cover) for your duvet cover set.

If you want to go bold for your bedroom, there are options aplenty. “We’re maximalists, so we say bump up the color and pattern no matter what your signature style is!” says Smith, adding that it’s important to still maintain balance. “If you have bold wallpaper, pull a color from it and go for a solid, textured duvet—like a rich velvet for drama or a soft linen for a more relaxed vibe. If you’re mixing patterns, think about scale—a bold, oversized print pairs best with a smaller, more delicate duvet pattern to give the eye a place to rest.”

If you don’t want to commit to one style just yet, rest assured that having a few duvets in rotation can help you keep your bedroom design fresh. “I tend to go simple on bedding and let the accessories be the pops of pattern and color that’s easily swapped out,” adds Fisher.

Maintenance: While these are great design accessories for a bedroom, they also need to be practical. Ashley Ross, founder and principal designer of Muse Noire Interiors recommends keeping these questions in mind when shopping: How does it fasten (zipper, tie up, or buttons)? Does it fit within your washer and dryer? This will help you know how to use it and how to care for it.

We tested the best duvet covers the same way we test products for the rest of our sleep content: by bringing the items in our homes and dressing them on our beds. This way, you’re guaranteed to get a real-life look at how the products perform after weeks and months of everyday use. We also wash them routinely to keep an eye out for any wear and tear. All of the brands we feature reflect a variety of price points, designs, and materials so you have the best options to choose from for your bedroom.

Jump to the “How We Tested” section of this article to watch an in-depth video about our testing methodology and some of our favorite products and brands.

You don’t necessarily need a duvet cover. It depends on how you like to dress your bed. In my opinion, it’s a great bed accessory. A duvet cover not only protects your duvet insert but it also gives you the opportunity to easily switch up your bedscape (instead of swapping comforters when you want a new look). That said, pay attention to the care instructions for your insert because some do not recommend washing or dry cleaning.

There are several ways you can put a duvet cover on, but according to TikTok experts, this method below is as foolproof as possible:

Start by turning your duvet cover inside out, top side down, with the duvet opener at the foot of the bed. Then, place your comforter on top and secure the corners with the attached ties to the duvet cover. Starting at the head of the bed, roll the duvet down towards the foot just like a burrito. Finally, fold the duvet opening over each end of the roll, and unroll the blanket back towards the

Always check the manufacturer instructions to find out how to wash your specific duvet cover. However, the most common way to clean a duvet cover is by machine washing it with like colors with a gentle detergent on a cold cycle. If the duvet cover has a zipper closure, it's usually helpful to zip it closed to keep it from snagging in the washing machine.

It's generally recommended to wash your duvet cover as often as you wash your sheets, which is about once a week. If you use a top sheet, though, you can usually extend another week and wash your duvet cover every other week.

Our editors selected top products in this story from tried-and-true brands on the market, from Brooklinen to Boll & Branch. These brands boast organic materials like 100% organic cotton and European Flax and bamboo for a sustainably made bed. Plus, many boast eco-friendly certifications like GOTS and Oeko-Tex so you know they are free of chemicals. As a design editor, I also made sure all of the products have a range of colors, patterns, and prints to complement a bedroom’s style.

#4879. US regulators move ahead on crypto trust charters as Senate scrutiny grows

Coinbase’s trust company received final clearance as lawmakers seek records on crypto firms’ compliance and potential conflicts of interest.

Federal regulators are opening more avenues for crypto companies to operate under US rules, while congressional investigators are asking to see the records behind those decisions. Lawmakers want to know how regulators justified new trust charters, how crypto companies handled compliance and what dealings they had with people tied to President Donald Trump’s administration.

On Nov. 9, Coinbase announced that its national trust company had received final approval to open. The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency granted preliminary conditional approval in April. The company said the charter gives its custody business a consistent federal framework.

Lawmakers had been questioning how federal regulators were using their existing authority to expand crypto companies’ reach. In a May 18 letter to the OCC, Sen. Elizabeth Warren challenged at least nine crypto trust-charter approvals, including Coinbase’s earlier conditional approval. She asked for the applications, the legal analyses behind the approvals and any related communications between OCC officials and the White House or Trump family.

Four days before Coinbase’s announcement, Sen. Richard Blumenthal renewed demands for records from Binance, Tether and two Trump-linked ventures. He gave them until Jan. 4, 2027, to turn over the requested records voluntarily and warned that his subcommittee could take other steps to obtain them.

#4877. The 12 Best Underwear for Men, Tested by Style Editors

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

Boxer briefs from Mack Weldon and Calvin Klein came out on top in our testing.

I’VE WORN ENOUGH bad underwear to know it can sabotage your entire day. This is the layer that determines whether you’re comfortable or constantly readjusting before anything else goes on. And yet, most men stick with the same underwear type from college. Meanwhile, the category has evolved. Today’s best underwear is softer, stretchier, and far more breathable, with odor-fighting tech and support that cradles your crown jewels without the squeeze. If you haven’t upgraded lately, your top drawer is probably long overdue for a refresh.

At Men’s Health, we’ve been testing underwear since 2015, and I’ve personally cycled through more pairs than I can count—part of a larger pool spanning 50-plus brands and 100-plus styles, from newer names like Skims to longtime staples like Calvin Klein. Year after year, our biggest takeaway stays the same: the pairs worth buying stay put, feel smooth from morning to night, and remain in great shape after a few spins through the wash. Whether you’re a boxer-briefs guy, a loose-boxers loyalist, or somewhere in between, this is one piece you don’t want to get wrong.

Out of the hundreds of skivvies we've tested since 2018, the Airknitx Boxer Brief came out on top for its comfort, support, and breathability. I’ve worn it to work, during workout classes, and everywhere in between. One feature I appreciate is the supportive pouch, which comfortably cradles the family jewels without suffocating them. It skips the front fly that gives you quicker, easier access when using the bathroom, but the tradeoff is a cleaner, sharper fit. The polyamide-elastane fabric has a mesh-like texture that keeps you cool and dry, instead of soaking up sweat during intense movement. Even during a four-mile run on the treadmill, this pair never once felt overheated, swampy, or in a rush to change. The waist feels secure without rolling, while the grippy leg bands keep everything in place without squeezing your thighs.

Like the name suggests, the brief feels light as air. It’s insanely soft on the skin, and the cut is also flattering on the thighs for guys with beefy quads. To really seal the deal, Mack Weldon even incorporated mesh cool zones in the back to boost airflow and help prevent odors when temperatures climb. Overall, it’s a functional pair built for everything under the sun: daily wear, hot weather, sleeping, gym workouts, long-haul flights, outdoor adventures, and the list continues. Plus, there's a vast color selection of solids and heathers, which go with just about any casual and business casual fit.

Read More: Mack Weldon Airknitx Boxer Brief Review

Sometimes, sticking with an OG brand is the smartest move. And when it comes to underwear, it's impossible to fail with a pair from Calvin Klein. As the pioneer of sexy basics that won us over with celebrity campaigns, we love its stretch boxer brief for its seriously smooth cotton-spandex fabric.

Our testers say this boxer brief is super comfortable and breathable. The stretch is another big win. Gollayan has used this during leg day and yoga and found that the fabric moves well with every activity. Plus, he's been using these boxer briefs since 2022 and found that they look good as new after countless trips to the washing machine.

What makes CK's classic so popular is its ability to keep things sleek—it doesn't increase the bulk of your thighs in slim pants. The contoured pouch and mid-thigh length are comfortable and deliver ample support.

If what you do in a pair of undies involves a lot of moving, sweating, and calorie-burning, we highly recommend the UA Tech 6-inch Boxerjack Briefs, a pair of running underwear that packs a lot of features for guys with very active lifestyles. It has an anti-chafing feature, providing maximum comfort and fit, even if worn during athletic activities. And thanks to the neat polyester-spandex blend, these boxer briefs have a super breathable fabric, meaning you're receiving maximum airflow and comfort.

These boxer briefs proved themselves on active days too—holding things together during intense HIIT sessions without feeling noticeable on your thighs. In our testing, we found that the four-way stretch material moved easily with our legs and is breathable and ultra-soft to boot. But what truly makes it stand out is the extremely supportive design: The combination of a performance waistband and an articulated mesh fly panel and gusset keep your goods in place, no matter how hard you run.

Read More: Best Moisture-Wicking Underwear

The 4D Flex Microfiber mesh boxer briefs from Polo Ralph Lauren will keep you cool from sunup to sundown. Essentially, that's their objective and we found they follow through on it with a soft cotton-modal blend that's moisture-wicking to fend off swamp crotch and swamp ass. They do this while still maintaining a high level of everyday comfort with four-way stretch and breathability thanks to the side mesh panels.

Their slim silhouette feels like a second skin, and won't ride up or bunch up under your dress pants. That means you can wear them to work, the gym, or even around the house. In our testing, we also found the pouch and gusset to be supportive and comfortable.

In terms of cleaning, it can handle multiple cycles of washing, but drying is where the waistband has an issue. We recommend air drying or putting on a low-tumble dryer setting to help the elastic retain its shape as we've noticed it can lose its stretch on a couple rounds of high heat.

Kim Kardashian expanding her Skims into men's underwear might've been one of the best things to happen to our top drawers. The brand's Stretch collection, which I've been testing, nails that sweet spot between function and finesse. The fit is nothing short of chef's kiss, sculpted enough to look great under jeans and hold my crown jewels in place. It's the kind of boxer brief that's so comfy you almost forget you're wearing it, yet still gives you that sleek, athletic silhouette.

What really sets it apart is the stretch. It's tuned just right: never saggy, never constrictive, and it stays put whether I'm hitting the gym, playing tennis, or running errands. The cotton-modal-elastane blend has solid recovery, snapping back into shape after every wash and wear like it's brand new. The waistband never gave me any problems; it has this velvety texture that sits gently against your skin, so no digging or irritation.

And yeah, even with the celebrity name attached, the hype checks out. I've worn this brief under everything like chinos, joggers, running tights. Every time the takeaway is the same: You can barely feel it. Plus, the color selection is pretty broad with classic shades and limited-edition tones including deep chocolate, green, and desert tan.

The first thing that stood out to us with Abercrombie’s Boxer Brief is the old-school look, consisting of a solid color cotton with a white sewn-on waistband, subtly emblazoned with the brand’s logo. Speaking of which, the waistband sits comfortably without rolling down whether you're bending down to tie your shoes or stretching out across the bed. Plus, it stays put—meaning there are no awkward adjustments needed.

The cotton and elastane blend fabric has a soft washed feel that usually takes some time to break in new underwear. While it fits like a boxer brief should, it wasn’t tight like a compression short, providing a little wiggle room. If you’re a boxer brief guy and you need a quick, easy, and affordable refresh of your collection, this is the way to go. It comes in a five pack, each offering five distinct colors, with the exception of the all-black set. For the price, it’s also one of the best values we’ve come across in men’s underwear.

Tommy John earned the crown for the best overall pajamas due to their übersoft second-skin fabric, so it's no shock that the brand's underwear exceeds our expectations, too. What sets these apart from others is the micro modal and spandex blend, which feels unreal—like ridiculously smooth against the skin. We're talking a fabric so luxurious that it makes regular cotton feel rough in comparison. Based on our testing, this pair of trunks nails the perfect balance of stretch and structure with their four-way stretch, so they move with you no matter how active (or lazy) your day gets.

Unlike other trunks that call for constant tugging or readjusting, these stayed perfectly in place, whether we were sitting, standing, or running errands around town. The quick-draw fly makes using the bathroom easier and faster in the middle of the night. On humid days, these are a lifesaver. Despite us breaking a sweat, this underwear stayed fresh, which speaks to their exceptional level of odor resistance. And even after multiple washes, the softness doesn't diminish—a true sign of premium quality.

Sunspel’s Classic Boxer Shorts are hands down some of the best out there, and once you try them, you’ll get it. This pair is made by a U.K. brand with over a century of experience perfecting the essentials, so it's time-tested. These boxers are cut from long-staple cotton, meaning the fibers are longer, the fabric is softer, and it'll last for the long haul. Basically, it feels ridiculously comfortable—like you’re lounging in luxury every time you put it on—and it stays that way wear after wear.

One standout feature is the distinctive back panel. Sunspel uses a single smooth panel across the rear versus an uncomfortable central seam running down the middle. For us, that meant no chafing, no awkward pressure, and no irritation, even when we were sitting at our work desk or running quick errands. The fabric is lightweight but strong, so it breathes well and never bunches under pants. During testing, it held up all day, no matter what: long commutes, walking tours on vacation, or casual bike rides. We don't recommend wearing this pair under gym shorts, but you can reserve it for days of less sweat-inducing activity since it's all cotton.

They’ve got this easy, relaxed fit that gives you full range of motion, but the tailoring keeps them from feeling baggy or sloppy. And then there’s the design: They’re finished with a super gentle waistband that sits comfortably. We also love that there's solid colors as well as striped patterns. It's the kind that makes you rethink the whole category. They’re built for comfort but stylish enough to feel special, which is exactly what you want from a pair you’ll wear day in and day out.

I normally wouldn’t trust underwear that costs under $10 to compete with premium pairs, but Uniqlo’s trunks are the exception. The Japanese retailer offers some of the best basics around, delivering impressive quality at an affordable price, including these boxer shorts, which are especially comfortable in the heat. They’re made with a breathable woven cotton fabric, which feels much lighter than any knit underwear I own. When the temps went up to 100 degrees in New York last week, these kept me cool all day.

The fit is more open and roomy than my briefs, so my crown jewels had plenty of breathing room and even caught a breeze when I was lounging around. I also love how they lie flat under shorts and linen pants, though I would skip wearing slim trousers since the fabric can bunch. Even though the waistband is scrunched, it sits gently against my skin without causing any irritation. When my Sunspel pair is in the laundry, I’ll even wear it to bed on warm nights. For such an inexpensive style, it holds up over time. I’ve washed it multiple times without seeing a single loose seam or noticing any shrinkage. Plus, the striped pattern looks timeless, so it doesn’t feel like a bargain-bin underwear.

I can always count on mesh fabric to keep me cool when I need it most, which is why I love this underwear. SAXX uses a polyester-elastane mesh with an open, dotted texture that lets heat and moisture escape, so I never feel clammy. Even when I sweat, the fabric never gets waterlogged and dries incredibly fast. It’s one of my go-to pairs for workouts, especially on heavy cardio days. The hammock-style pouch keeps everything secure and supported while I’m biking or running on the treadmill, and the fit is snugger than most boxer shorts, specifically around the butt, thigh, and legs.

The 6-inch inseam stops mid-thigh, while the high waist sits right under your belly button. I can wear them under just about any pair of pants without worrying about bunching or visible lines. The compression-like fit may feel too snug if you prefer a roomier boxer short. And the mesh fabric isn’t as soft or natural-feeling as cotton or modal, so it may not be everyone’s favorite pair for lounging all day. The good thing is the pack of three can get you through half the week, especially if you stock up.

If you’re ready to upgrade from basic cotton underwear, CDLP is where I’d start. I love the Tencel Lyocell fabric that has an incredibly silky, almost cooling feel against my skin. It’s surprisingly breathable, too, so I never feel overheated on days when the temps spike to 90 degrees. It strikes a nice balance between feeling luxurious and being practical. The snug fit hugs my body without squeezing too tightly. It rests just below the waist and has a 3.8-inch inseam that sits high on the upper thigh and hides under my short shorts. Some of the more expensive pairs tend to pill, but the fabric on this one keeps its smooth, premium feel even after multiple washes. The only real drawback is the price, but if you’re willing to splurge on a single pair of underwear, the comfort makes it feel well worth it.

Quality underwear doesn't have to cost a fortune. Take Uniqlo's Airism Ultra Seamless Boxer Briefs, which clock in under $20 and also fit like a glove. During my testing, the cutoff waist felt invisible, sitting flush against the skin without squeezing or rolling, like it was made just for me. Despite its close-hugging cut, there's a fair amount of stretch to accommodate you running up the stairs, twisting in your chair, or walking briskly through crowded city streets.

Overall, I found this pair to be lightweight, super breathable, and packed with new moisture-wicking technology that helps to keep you fresh, cool, and dry around the clock. Whether it's a hot day or you're working up a sweat at the gym, Airism pulls moisture away from your skin, making sure you don't feel swampy down under.

Every Sunday at my house is wash day, but this underwear has survived through every last cycle without losing its allure. Our only gripe is that Uniqlo Airism sells out very fast, which means you have to wait for the occasional restock—so get them now.

Cotton is the OG of underwear fabrics, and our testers found that it's the most comfortable knit for everyday fits. Take note: while cotton is pretty breathable, it doesn't do a great job of wicking away moisture. That's why our fashion editors do not recommend cotton skivvies for working out. In some cases, a pair of undies that's 100% cotton tends to lose shape over time and can give a swamp-ass feeling. If you have money to spend, we recommend trying a long-staple or organic cotton, which is more premium and durable.

Nylon is moisture-wicking and super durable, so the fabric won’t pill or stretch out. However, a little spandex (aka elastane) in the fabric helps for movement and extra comfort. Plus, it dries quickly too, so you won't feel sticky post-workout.

Imagine cotton, but smoother and a little fancier. Modal has a silky-soft feel that's light and cool against your skin. Testers say their favorite modal boxer briefs almost disappear under their clothes.

If you're looking to keep your precious cargo secure, then briefs provide the most security. However, if you want to let the package breathe, then boxers are your best bet. Remember: Boxers tend to ride up when you're wearing slim pants, which is why we recommend only wearing them with more relaxed fits.

If you need extra support, we recommend underwear with a pouch or a snugger fit around the waistband. For some men with testicular pain or discomfort, they may want to find a style that fits well and doesn't ride up or bunch, as this could aggravate their symptoms.

Your underwear is the first thing you put on and the last thing you take off, so it has to work with you, not against you, all day long. If it doesn't do its job, you'll feel it, whether it's discomfort, chafing, or overheating.

Think about it: excellent underwear isn't just about looking cool (though that's like icing on the cake). It's about how it performs in real life. Are you lounging at home? Going for a long run? Stuck on a flight for hours? Each of these scenarios demands something different. You need underwear that supports your lifestyle, whether that's stretch for flexibility, moisture-wicking for sweat, or breathability to keep things fresh down yonder.

The best breathable underwear manages heat and moisture so sweat can escape instead of getting trapped against your skin. Many use micro-knit or mesh-like weaves that create tiny air channels within the fabric, allowing heat to dissipate and air to circulate as you move. Others incorporate moisture-wicking fibers to pull sweat away from the body and spread it across the surface of the fabric so it evaporates faster. Some brands even add targeted “cool zones” or thinner panels in high-sweat areas to boost airflow where you need it most.

When underwear can’t breathe, moisture builds up, leading to overheating, chafing, irritation, and odor. Breathable underwear works with your body by keeping things cooler, drier, and more comfortable throughout the day. For Men’s Health guys, breathability makes a difference for everyday wear, long commutes, desk jobs, workouts, travel days, and humid conditions. It’s especially clutch for guys who sweat easily, live in hot climates, train hard, or spend long stretches in the same pair from morning to night.

As part of the Men’s Health style team, led by our Style and Reviews Director Christian Gollayan, I’ve tested some of the best—and worst—underwear on the market firsthand. Since 2015, our team has worn, washed, and stressed-tested more than 100 pairs across every major style, brand, and fabric imaginable, from classic cotton briefs to high-tech performance boxer briefs and luxe everyday upgrades.

Testing wasn't limited to just one body type or fit preference. In addition to my own wear tests, multiple Men's Health editors with different builds pitched in, spanning sizes from small through XXL. This allowed us to see how each pair fit and performed across a wide range of body types, rises, thigh sizes, and proportions—and to flag issues like inconsistent sizing, rolling waistbands, or fabric that only works on one kind of frame.

I wore each pair repeatedly in real-life situations, including workdays, workouts, commutes, travel, and weekend outings. I looked at how each pair performed over time, paying close attention to whether fabrics remained soft without pilling, waistbands held their shape, seams avoided chafing, and support held up after hours of movement. I judged each pair on fabric quality, fit, breathability, odor control, stretch and recovery, durability after repeated washes, and comfort levels ranging from morning to night. Only the pairs that consistently delivered comfort, support, and long-term performance earned a spot on this list. What you’ll find here are the top 12 best men’s underwear options that rose to the top after years of hands-on testing by the Men’s Health team.

Boxers: They’re classic, loose-fitting shorts that are lightweight, with lots of breathing room, and zero restriction. They’re great for lounging or sleeping because they feel airy and relaxed, but that same looseness makes them less practical under slim pants. Fabric can bunch, ride up, and offer little to no support if you’re moving around a lot. Boxer briefs: They’re cut like boxers but fit snugly like briefs. That means they hug your thighs, hold everything in place, and layer smoothly under jeans, trousers, or even gym shorts. They also prevent chafing since the fabric creates a barrier between your thighs—a lifesaver if you walk a lot or hit the gym. The tradeoff? They’re less airy than boxers, but most guys prefer the balance of comfort, coverage, and support.

That really depends on your laundry schedule. If you’re someone who does laundry once a week, aim for at least 10 to 12 pairs so you’ve got a little cushion. If laundry happens less often—say every two weeks—you’ll probably want 15 to 20 pairs. If you’re very active, then consider stocking your drawer with 25 to 30 pairs. Basically, you want enough to last until wash day plus a couple extra for workouts, surprise trips, or the occasional lazy Sunday when you just don’t feel like doing laundry.

A good rule of thumb: it’s reasonable to refresh your stash every six to 12 months, but quality underwear can last longer depending on fabric, frequency of wear, washing, and condition. If the elastic’s shot, they’re sagging, developing holes, or the fabric’s thinning, that’s your cue to toss them. Think of it as a rotation—you don’t need to replace everything at once, but gradually swap in new pairs so you’re always stocked with comfortable, supportive ones.

Every man has worn them at some point; boxers are light and loose and so freeing. They're the classic underwear style for men that feels very relaxed with short legs. This type of underwear is perfect for lounging around the house, sleeping, or wearing under relaxed-fit pants. Also comes in a variety of prints and patterns (hello, personality).

Think speedo. Think upside-down triangle. Briefs provide the required coverage and optimal support while exposing more skin for ease of mobility. Here, there's no risk of leg fabric riding up (because there's none).

Perhaps the most popular one, it's a hybrid of loose-fit boxers and tight briefs, offering a solid balance of support and comfort. If you’re not a fan of underwear that rides up too high, go for boxer briefs that have a longer leg and a snug fit, like compression underwear that’s perfect for the gym. They should skim the leg versus squeezing you too tight.

Like the title says, a trunk is similar to boxer briefs but with a shorter cut—halfway up the thigh. It's best for guys who want something fitted but less fabric around the leg. For some visual assistance, think of trunks as the underwear style that most CK models wear on big billboards.

It depends on personal preference, comfort, and the activity. Here's a quick breakdown to help guide your choice, weighing the pros and cons of both.

Tight underwear (e.g., briefs, boxer briefs) provides better support, which is especially useful for physical activities like running or working out. This type reduces chafing and prevents excessive movement, which can help with comfort throughout the day. Works well under slim-fit pants, as it avoids bunching and creates a cleaner silhouette. If it's too tight, it can restrict airflow and potentially cause discomfort or sweating, especially in warmer weather. Overly tight fits might not be ideal for guys concerned about reproductive health, though the effect is typically negligible with properly sized underwear.

On the other hand, loose underwear is better suited for lounging or casual, low-impact activities since it allows more airflow and freedom of movement. It feels more breathable, making it ideal for hotter climates or relaxed settings. Also, loose underwear can be paired with loose-fit pants for added comfort. This option lacks support, which feel uncomfortable during workouts or physical activity. Plus, it can cramp your style—bunching up under tighter pants and offering a restrictive feel.

If you want to protect the structural integrity of your underwear's waistband, the best way to keep them from stretching is to hand wash them and hang them dry. But given how impractical that is, the second best option is to put them in the washing machine on cold water and use a low dryer setting so the elastic doesn't warp. However, our testers say that most of the pairs they've tried have kept their waistbands' shapes even after several trips to the laundromat. If your underwear's waistband has lost its shape, you're probably overdue to replace it.

Even the best underwear won’t last if you don’t take care of it properly. Washing underwear inside out helps remove sweat and bacteria more effectively while protecting the fabric’s surface. Cold or warm water is usually best, as hot water can break down elastic fibers and cause shrinkage over time. Skip harsh detergents and fabric softeners, especially for performance or moisture-wicking underwear. Softeners can coat fibers and reduce breathability and odor control. When possible, air-drying is ideal, as high heat from dryers is the fastest way to kill stretch and warp waistbands. If you do use a dryer, stick to low heat.
